notes: Compiled by web research for engineering-validation only. Many primary standard texts (EN 716-1, EN 747-1/2, EN 1725, ASTM F1821) are paywalled; values from them here are taken from secondary summaries (manufacturer/test-lab articles) unless marked primary:true. Cross-check against a purchased standard before using as a pass/fail gate in the product.

rules.appliesTo: cot side slats (EN 716-1, children's cots for domestic use)
rules.sourceTitle: Baby Cot & Mattress Safety Standards of BS EN 716 (Picket&Rail)
rules.notes: Secondary summary. A second secondary source (search-engine synthesis, no stable URL) claimed 45-65mm instead — the two summaries conflict. EN 716-1 full text not accessible; treat both as unverified until the standard itself is read. Not used as a pass/fail gate without confirmation.

rules.appliesTo: gap between mattress and cot frame/sides (EN 716-1)
rules.sourceTitle: Baby Cot & Mattress Safety Standards of BS EN 716 (Picket&Rail)
rules.notes: Widely repeated figure (30 mm) across secondary cot-safety articles for EN 716-1; standard text not read directly.

rules.appliesTo: corner post / protrusion height above cot rail top (EN 716-1)
rules.sourceTitle: Baby Cot & Mattress Safety Standards of BS EN 716 (Picket&Rail)
rules.notes: Secondary; commonly cited 8 mm limit for cot corner posts/knobs (catch/strangulation hazard on clothing).

rules.valueText: edges and protrusions accessible in normal use must be rounded or chamfered, free of burrs and sharp edges; no radius given
rules.appliesTo: cots (EN 716-1)
rules.sourceTitle: EN 716-1 testing standard summary (Furnitest)
rules.notes: Qualitative requirement only; no numeric radius found in any accessible source. Not verified.

rules.appliesTo: rigid completely-bound openings in bunk/high beds (EN 747-1:2024)
rules.sourceTitle: BS EN 747-1:2024 preview (ANSI webstore) / secondary synthesis
rules.clause: EN 747-1:2024 (opening rule), tested per EN 747-2:2024 §5.2.2 probe / §6.3.1 procedure
rules.notes: "No accessible completely bound opening in rigid material with diameter/width >7mm and <12mm, unless depth <10mm or the EN 747-2 §5.2.2 probe enters." This is the classic pan-European finger-entrapment rule also used in EN 1129 (folding mechanisms) and similar furniture standards; reproduced from a secondary synthesis of the 2024 standard, not the purchased text.

rules.appliesTo: gaps adjacent to inner surface of side/end rails (EN 747-1:2024)
rules.sourceTitle: EN 747-1:2024 fact-check (GP Camping Guide)
rules.notes: Secondary summary; matches general pattern of EN furniture standards (small gaps near rigid rails capped near 20-25mm to block limb entrapment).

rules.appliesTo: gap between slats/railing components, general (EN 747-1:2024)
rules.sourceTitle: EN 747-1:2024 fact-check (GP Camping Guide)
rules.notes: "No body part may pass through or get caught." Secondary summary of the standard.

rules.appliesTo: top of mattress relative to top of fall-protection guardrail (EN 747-1:2024)
rules.sourceTitle: EN 747-1:2024 fact-check (GP Camping Guide)
rules.notes: i.e. guardrail must rise >=160mm above mattress top. Secondary summary.

rules.appliesTo: upper mattress height above floor that triggers EN 747-1 bunk/high-bed rules
rules.sourceTitle: EN 747-1:2024 fact-check (GP Camping Guide)
rules.notes: A Montessori floor bed (mattress at/near floor) is well below this threshold, so EN 747-1 does not apply to it directly -- relevant to why floor beds fall outside cot/bunk-bed standards.

rules.appliesTo: bunk bed ladder rung spacing (EN 747-1:2024)
rules.sourceTitle: EN 747-1:2024 fact-check (GP Camping Guide)
rules.notes: Not applicable to floor bed (no ladder). Kept for completeness only.

rules.appliesTo: US bunk beds: gap between guardrail and bed end structure (16 CFR 1213)
rules.sourceTitle: 16 CFR 1213.3 - Requirements (Cornell LII, e-CFR text)
rules.notes: 0.22 in = 5.6mm. Mandatory US federal rule for bunk beds, not toddler/floor beds, but a useful conservative reference for finger-entrapment gaps near a rigid guardrail-to-frame joint.

rules.appliesTo: US bunk beds: max distance from guardrail end to nearest bed-end structure (16 CFR 1213)
rules.sourceTitle: 16 CFR 1213.3 - Requirements (Cornell LII, e-CFR text)

rules.appliesTo: US bunk beds: guardrail top above mattress top surface (16 CFR 1213)
rules.sourceTitle: 16 CFR 1213.3 - Requirements (Cornell LII, e-CFR text)
rules.notes: 5 in = 130mm (127mm exact). Same 5-inch figure is repeated for US toddler beds (ASTM F1821) by multiple secondary sources -- see astm_f1821_guardrail_height_min.

rules.appliesTo: US bunk beds: end-structure height above mattress top for >=50% of bunk width, where no guardrail present (16 CFR 1213)
rules.sourceTitle: 16 CFR 1213.3 - Requirements (Cornell LII, e-CFR text)
rules.notes: 5 in = 130mm.

rules.appliesTo: US bunk beds: openings between bunks must either block a standard wedge-block probe or allow passage of a rigid sphere of this diameter (16 CFR 1213)
rules.sourceTitle: 16 CFR 1213.3 - Requirements (Cornell LII, e-CFR text)
rules.notes: 9 in = 230mm rigid sphere. Consistent with the general CPSC head-entrapment doctrine of 89-230mm (3.5-9in) being the hazardous zone (opening too big for torso/head to pass safely, too small to pass a head through freely) -- see cpsc_generic_head_entrapment_zone.

rules.appliesTo: US full-size baby cribs: distance between slats, spindles, corner posts, rods at any point (16 CFR 1508, FHSA)
rules.sourceTitle: CPSC Investigation Guideline - Structural Entrapment (Appendix 35, rev. Dec 2004)
rules.clause: 16 CFR 1508 (cribs); test detail 1508.11 for cutouts/partially-bounded openings
rules.notes: 2 3/8 in = 60.3mm. Applies to cribs, not floor beds or toddler beds, but is the primary numeric anchor for the 'gap large enough to trap limb/torso, small enough to trap head' logic used across US juvenile-product rules.

rules.appliesTo: General CPSC entrapment-hazard doctrine: 'an opening may present an entrapment hazard if the distance between two opposite surfaces is greater than 3.5in but less than 9in' (playground equipment, and used by analogy for other juvenile products' partially/fully bounded openings)
rules.sourceTitle: CPSC Investigation Guideline - Structural Entrapment (Appendix 35, rev. Dec 2004)
rules.clause: Cites ASTM F1487-01 (playground equipment) and ASTM F1148-03 (home playground equipment)
rules.notes: This exact range is codified for playground equipment (ASTM F1487/F1148), not explicitly for toddler/floor beds. The same CPSC document confirms ASTM F1821 (toddler beds) targets 'head and neck entrapment in end structures, between guard and side rails, and in mattress supports' but does not reproduce F1821's own numeric thresholds (standard is paywalled). Use this range only as a design heuristic, not a certified pass criterion, until F1821 text is obtained.

rules.appliesTo: US toddler bed definition: must accept a full-size crib mattress of at least 51-5/8in x 27-1/4in (16 CFR 1217 / ASTM F1821)
rules.sourceTitle: 16 CFR 1217.2 - Requirements for toddler beds (eCFR/Cornell LII paraphrase)
rules.notes: 1310mm x 690mm (1.31m x 0.69m). Also: intended for a child not less than 15 months old and not more than 50 lb (22.7kg).

rules.appliesTo: US toddler beds: guardrail top above the manufacturer's recommended sleeping surface (ASTM F1821 / 16 CFR 1217)
rules.sourceTitle: Federal Register 2011-9421 discussion (secondary search synthesis); corroborated by multiple secondary blogs (FlexiSpot, Craft-Child)
rules.clause: not confirmed against F1821 text itself (paywalled)
rules.notes: 5 in = 127mm, same figure as the bunk-bed rule (16 CFR 1213/ASTM F1427). Federal Register preamble text (per search synthesis, page itself blocked from direct fetch) states the rule is based on a 6in-thick mattress assumption if no max thickness is stated by the manufacturer. Could not independently verify by reading F1821 or the FR notice directly -- flagged medium confidence, not primary-verified.

rules.valueText: 90 ppm (0.009%) lead in surface coatings; 100 ppm (0.01%) total lead in any accessible component
rules.appliesTo: US toddler beds (16 CFR 1217 referencing CPSIA lead limits, not F1821-specific)
rules.sourceTitle: JJR Lab - How to get a 16 CFR Part 1217 Test Report
rules.clause: general CPSIA lead limits (16 CFR 1303 / 15 U.S.C. 1278a), applied to toddler beds via 1217
rules.notes: These are the general US CPSIA children's-product lead limits, not unique to F1821; secondary source may conflate them with F1821-specific numbers.

rules.appliesTo: Israeli standard TI 4007 Part 1 (bunk/high beds for domestic use, based on EN 747-1 family): guardrail height above bed base, mattress excluded
rules.sourceTitle: Web-search synthesis of Israeli Standards Institution (SII) bunk-bed guidance page
rules.notes: Mandatory Israeli standard by law for bunk/high beds. Could not fetch the SII page directly (fetch attempt failed); value is from a search-engine synthesis of the page, not confirmed by direct read. Scope: applies to beds where the lower level sits >=800mm above the floor -- a Montessori floor bed at/near floor level would NOT be covered by this standard.

rules.appliesTo: Israeli TI 4007-1: spacing between upper surfaces of adjacent bunk-bed ladder steps
rules.sourceTitle: Web-search synthesis of Israeli Standards Institution (SII) bunk-bed guidance page
rules.notes: Not applicable to a floor bed (no ladder); kept for completeness. Not directly verified.

rules.appliesTo: Israeli TI 4007-1 scope threshold: applies to bunk beds or beds whose lower level is 800mm or more above the floor
rules.sourceTitle: Web-search synthesis of Israeli Standards Institution (SII) bunk-bed guidance page
rules.notes: Confirms Montessori floor beds (mattress near floor) fall outside this Israeli mandatory standard's scope.

rules.appliesTo: Israeli standard TI 1548 (mandatory): infant/toddler bed mattress thickness
rules.sourceTitle: Israeli Standards Institution - infant mattress standard page (search synthesis)
rules.notes: 7-15cm. Rationale given: thick enough for comfort/safety, thin enough that the toddler cannot climb/fall out unassisted. Mattresses over 10cm thick must be labeled 'for use in beds taller than 60cm'.

rules.appliesTo: Israeli TI 1548: minimum bed side height required if mattress thickness exceeds 100mm
rules.sourceTitle: Israeli Standards Institution - infant mattress standard page (search synthesis)
rules.notes: Directly relevant: a Montessori floor bed with a mattress thicker than 100mm and side rails lower than 600mm would fall outside what TI 1548 assumes safe (product-owner decision needed on rail height vs. mattress thickness combinations).

rules.appliesTo: General US crib-safety guidance (not a specific standard clause): gap between mattress edge and frame should not fit more than two adult fingers side by side
rules.sourceTitle: Multiple crib-safety blogs (secondary synthesis, e.g. hiccapop, mamazing)
rules.notes: Popular consumer rule-of-thumb (~25mm/1in), not a verified standard clause. Provided for comparison with the EN 716-1 30mm figure above; the two are of the same order of magnitude.

rules.appliesTo: Common cot/toddler mattress size sold in Israel and Europe: 60x120cm
rules.sourceTitle: IKEA Israel children's mattresses category page
rules.notes: IKEA Israel's own listed children's mattress sizes at time of research were 70x160cm and 80x200cm (UNDERLIG, PLUTTEN, VIMSIG, NATTSMYG, INNERLIG); 60x120cm was reported by generic (non-Israel-specific) sources as a common cot-to-toddler size in Europe. Treat 60x120 as plausible but not confirmed for the Israeli market specifically.

rules.appliesTo: IKEA Israel junior/toddler mattress size (UNDERLIG)
rules.sourceTitle: IKEA Israel children's mattresses category page
rules.notes: Directly observed on IKEA Israel's site via fetch (product listing), not a standard.

rules.appliesTo: IKEA Israel child mattress size (PLUTTEN, VIMSIG, NATTSMYG, INNERLIG)
rules.sourceTitle: IKEA Israel children's mattresses category page
rules.notes: Directly observed on IKEA Israel's site via fetch (product listing), not a standard.

rules.appliesTo: Standard Israeli single/youth mattress size (90x190cm), typical next step after toddler bed
rules.sourceTitle: mizran.co.il - mattress size guide
rules.notes: Retailer source; 90x190cm described as the standard Israeli single-mattress size (80x190cm also common); 90x200cm exists but is described as non-standard/less common.

rules.valueText: up to 110 kg assumed user mass for strength/durability force calculations
rules.appliesTo: EN 1725:2023 domestic beds (adult beds; explicitly excludes bunk beds, high beds, medical beds, water/air beds)
rules.sourceTitle: SATRA - Safety, strength and durability testing of beds to EN 1725:2023
rules.notes: No Newton values for the actual static/impact loads on frame, mattress support, or edges were found in any accessible secondary source; the standard text itself is paywalled. Load in Newtons is NOT VERIFIED -- do not fabricate a number for the engine.

rules.appliesTo: EN 1725:2023 electrically-operated (adjustable) beds only
rules.sourceTitle: Catas - EN 1725:2023 FAQs
rules.notes: Not applicable to a static Montessori floor bed (no mechanism).

rules.valueText: EN 1725 explicitly does not apply to bunk beds, high beds, or medical beds (separate standards exist for these); it targets adult domestic beds generally
rules.appliesTo: scope boundary
rules.sourceTitle: SATRA - Safety, strength and durability testing of beds to EN 1725:2023
rules.notes: No EN standard specifically targets a low, floor-level children's bed frame; this is the core reason floor beds are a standards gap requiring a product-owner decision on which combination of standards (or which parts of EN 716/747/1725/ASTM F1821) to voluntarily follow.

rules.valueText: WHO Child Growth Standards, 50th percentile (median) body weight, approx.: 1y ~9.6-10.2kg, 2y ~12.2-12.5kg, 3y ~14.3kg, 4y ~16.3kg, 5y ~18.3-18.5kg (boys slightly higher than girls throughout)
rules.appliesTo: design child mass by age, for structural load assumptions on a toddler/child floor bed
rules.sourceTitle: WHO Child Growth Standards - Weight-for-age, boys and girls 0-5 years (percentile tables)
rules.notes: Numbers above are paraphrased from a search-engine summary of the official WHO PDF tables (not independently re-read cell by cell) -- re-verify exact figures directly from the PDF before hard-coding. For a structural safety margin, engine should use a considerably higher mass than the median (e.g. a high percentile, or an adult-comparable value for a used/misused product) rather than the median child mass alone -- product-owner decision needed on target percentile and margin.

rules.appliesTo: toys and (by common design practice, not by direct standard citation) children's furniture edges: EN 71-1 / ISO 8124-1 sharp-edge test uses a mandrel of this radius; an edge is 'sharp' (fails) if it cuts adhesive tape wrapped on the mandrel to a length >=13mm in one 360 degree pass
rules.sourceTitle: TestingLab / GESTER sharp-edge test method summaries
rules.clause: EN 71-1 / ISO 8124-1 sharp edge test method (secondary summary)
rules.notes: This is a TOY standard test, not a furniture standard. No EN 716/747 furniture-specific edge-radius NUMBER was found (those standards only require edges to be 'rounded or chamfered, free of burrs' qualitatively). Using the toy 2mm mandrel / no-sharp-edge criterion as a design proxy is a product decision, not a verified furniture-standard requirement.

rules.valueText: Category III (scraped-off coating material) migration limits, mg/kg: Lead 160, Cadmium 17, Chromium(III) 460, Chromium(VI) 0.2, Antimony 560
rules.appliesTo: coatings/paints/finishes on children's products (EN 71-3, Table 2)
rules.sourceTitle: EN 71-3:2013+A1 full text (public-domain mirror)
rules.notes: Read from an actual (older, 2013+A1) edition of the standard text, so treated as primary for that edition. Current edition is EN 71-3:2019+A2:2024 -- re-verify these table values are unchanged before relying on them; some element limits were tightened across EN 71-3 revisions (e.g. additions of organic tin, aluminium in 2019 versions).

rules.valueText: E1 class: formaldehyde emission <= 0.124 mg/m3 (approx. 0.1 ppm) chamber concentration
rules.appliesTo: wood-based panels (MDF, particleboard, plywood) under EN 13986, tested per EN 717-1
rules.sourceTitle: Arcedior - E1 vs E0 Formaldehyde Board Standards
rules.notes: Widely and consistently reported figure across independent secondary sources. EU is reportedly moving to a stricter 'E1-EF' limit (roughly half of E1) starting August 2026 per one secondary source -- not independently confirmed, flag for re-check before committing to E1 as the long-term target.

rules.appliesTo: hardwood plywood (veneer core or composite core), US TSCA Title VI / CARB Phase 2
rules.sourceTitle: 40 CFR 770.10 - Formaldehyde emission standards (Cornell LII e-CFR text)
rules.notes: Test method ASTM E1333-14 (large chamber) per the regulation.

rules.appliesTo: particleboard, US TSCA Title VI / CARB Phase 2
rules.sourceTitle: 40 CFR 770.10 - Formaldehyde emission standards (Cornell LII e-CFR text)
rules.notes: Same value as EN 622-5 particleboard citation already in ENGINEERING_DATA.md context -- consistent across regimes.

rules.appliesTo: medium-density fiberboard, US TSCA Title VI / CARB Phase 2
rules.sourceTitle: 40 CFR 770.10 - Formaldehyde emission standards (Cornell LII e-CFR text)

rules.appliesTo: thin medium-density fiberboard (<=8mm thickness), US TSCA Title VI / CARB Phase 2
rules.sourceTitle: 40 CFR 770.10 - Formaldehyde emission standards (Cornell LII e-CFR text)

rules.valueText: CPSC recalled ~7,450 units of Zipadee Kids convertible house-bed frames / Montessori floor beds (2018-2021 production) because spindle spacing let a child's torso pass through but not the head, an entrapment/strangulation hazard. No specific mm value published in the recall notice.
rules.appliesTo: Montessori floor bed / house-frame products specifically
rules.sourceTitle: CPSC Recall: Zipadee Kids Recalls Convertible House Bed Frames and Montessori Floor Beds
rules.notes: Real-world precedent confirming spindle/rail spacing is the dominant hazard specifically named for this product category; no standard is cited as having been violated in the notice itself, underscoring that floor beds/house frames sit in a regulatory gap in the US too.

rules.appliesTo: general mattress-industry guidance (not a safety standard): max center-to-center or clear gap between bed-base slats to avoid sag/damage
rules.sourceTitle: Puffy - How Far Apart Should Bed Slats Be? Spacing Guide
rules.notes: 2-3in (51-76mm) commonly cited as max for general mattresses; foam/latex/hybrid mattresses recommended <=70mm (2.75in), innerspring tolerates up to ~102mm (4in). Manufacturer marketing guidance, not a certified standard -- treat as a product decision input for the slat-spacing default, not a compliance requirement.

rules.valueText: A single bed slat spanning between two side rails, supporting a mattress, can be modeled as a simply supported beam under distributed (mattress + body weight tributary strip) or central point load, same method already used in this project's shelf/beam engine (EN 1995-1-1 style deflection/bending checks).
rules.appliesTo: slat engineering check methodology
rules.sourceTitle: calcresource - Simple beam deflection formulas (already cited in project ENGINEERING_DATA.md)
rules.notes: Not a safety-standard citation but a valid, already-used-in-project engineering method. Load case should represent worst case tributary body-weight strip on the slat nearest the child's center of mass, using a design mass per the WHO figures above and an explicit product-owner-chosen safety margin, since no standard gives a bed-slat point load in Newtons directly.
